assertions.description: Iterator.prototype.join is a function (the proposal's single surface).
Iterator.prototype.join has length 1 and name "join" per the standard built-in function rules.
An undefined separator joins with a single comma: [1,2,3].values().join() is "1,2,3".
Joining an already-exhausted or empty iterator returns the empty string, not undefined and not a throw.
undefined and null elements contribute the empty string but still receive separators: [1,undefined,null,2] joined with "|" is "1|||2".
A non-string separator is coerced with ToString: joining [1,2] with the number 0 yields "102".
A Symbol separator throws TypeError because ToString(Symbol) is disallowed (guarded so a browser without the method fails instead of vacuously passing).
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof Iterator === "undefined" || typeof Iterator.prototype.join !== "function") return false; try { [1,2].values().join(Symbol("sep")); return false; } catch (err) { return err instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: Calling Iterator.prototype.join on a non-object receiver throws TypeError (guarded so a browser without the method fails instead of vacuously passing).
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof Iterator === "undefined" || typeof Iterator.prototype.join !== "function") return false; try { Iterator.prototype.join.call(5, ","); return false; } catch (err) { return err instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: join drains its receiver: after joining, the iterator's next() reports done and a second join returns "".
assertions.test: (() => { const it = [1,2].values(); const first = it.join(); return first === "1,2" && it.next().done === true && it.join() === ""; })()

assertions.description: When an element's ToString throws mid-stream, the error propagates and the underlying iterator is closed (a generator's finally block runs).
assertions.test: (() => { let closed = false; function* g() { try { yield { toString() { throw new RangeError("boom"); } }; yield 2; } finally { closed = true; } } const it = g(); try { it.join("-"); return false; } catch (err) { return err instanceof RangeError && closed === true; } })()

assertions.description: When ToString(separator) throws before iteration starts, the iterator is still closed: its return() method is invoked (IfAbruptCloseIterator).
assertions.test: (() => { let returnCalled = false; const it = { next() { return { value: 1, done: false }; }, return() { returnCalled = true; return { done: true }; } }; try { Iterator.prototype.join.call(it, { toString() { throw new RangeError("boom"); } }); return false; } catch (err) { return err instanceof RangeError && returnCalled === true; } })()
